card werk-board-control-archive-ends-build  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
The builder loop ends its own build when it reads that its ticket is archived
why: A build can run from the merge loop or from a single build command, and only the builder loop is present in both. When the builder loop reads the board itself, an archive ends every build the same way, with no second process that has to notice it.

While a build runs, its builder loop reads the board about once a second. When it finds its ticket archived during a pass, it stops the agent of that pass, commits nothing of the pass, runs no checks, records no retry, and ends. An archive that comes while the checks or the grader of the last pass run also ends the build: nothing of the build merges, even a pass that ended green. In every case the worktree folder goes and the ticket's branch stays.

A merge loop that started the build merges nothing of it and goes on with its other tickets. The archive ends one build. It is not a stop of the merge loop, so no other ticket moves back to ready.

Example:

- Ticket T "Draw the board" is in building. The agent of its pass 2 runs.
- Ticket U "Save the log" builds beside T in the same merge loop.
- A person archives T on the board.

1. The board log gets the archive. T leaves the columns.
2. Within about a second, the builder loop of T reads the board and sees T archived.
3. It stops the pass 2 agent. The board no longer shows T as running.
4. The builder loop of T ends. The branch of T stays. Nothing of T merges.
5. The merge loop goes on. U builds and merges as before.
6. Case where nothing happens: the person cancels the confirmation. No event is written, and the build of T goes on.

```
board log            builder loop of T              agent of T, pass 2
---------            -----------------              ------------------
T archived  ---->    reads board (~1 s): archived
                     stop  ---------------------->  stopped
                     no commit, no checks
                     worktree removed, branch kept
                          |
                          v
                     merge loop: T merges nothing; U goes on
```

~1 s: the time between two reads of the board.

card werk-board-control  [decided]
A person reorders, archives, and triggers the build of one ticket at a time
why: Build order is a person's choice while the process is iterative (#st-iterative), and a manual trigger keeps that choice in their hands.
subtree: 3 cards, 3 decided

Four direct actions on the board:

1. Reorder tickets within ready.
2. Archive a ticket. A ready, blocked or building ticket shows this action; a merging or done ticket does not. Archiving a building ticket ends its build and keeps its branch. Archiving asks for confirmation first, and the confirmation says the ticket is never deleted for good — an agent can restore it, the same reversible pattern #werk-remove already uses for a map card.
3. Trigger the build of a ready ticket inside an active run. Either press the trigger icon, or drag the ticket into building.
4. A triggered build cannot be stopped in place. A person ends it by archiving its ticket (action 2), and nothing else returns a building ticket to ready.

The drag from ready into building is the only manual column-to-column move. Every other move is not a person
